$comment: A run that wrote a document with no risk register at all: an executive summary, a coverage plan, and no
table carrying a risk id and a score.
It is in the corpus because a document the harness cannot read must be refused rather than scored as a
register with nothing wrong in it. Every ratio over an empty register is either 0 over 0 or vacuously
perfect, and a run that produced nothing would otherwise report clean. The refusal is an environment
failure at exit 2, which is a different claim from a measured quality failure at exit 1.
It is also the one case that holds the contract's run-measured oracle to the same answer: the oracle
finds no R-NNN in any table cell, so it refuses the run the harness refuses.
derivation: readDesign parses the tables, finds none carrying both a risk id column and a score column, and returns
environment-parser with the reason that the document carries no such table. No scored object is produced,
so the stored result is the failure class and nothing else.
The coverage table in the document has a Test Level column and no Risk Link column, which is the P3 shape
the template ships. It is not a risk register and the parser does not treat it as one.
`banded` is now `rows` on every case, because a row under a heading that declares no score range is a
band failure rather than an exemption. `cleanControl` is `ceiling` and both sets declare one, so the
seeded corpus is bounded too. `grounding` carries `topSeverityMissed`, the count of the set's
lowest-ranked risks that went unreported. Material risks are assigned by maximum matching rather than
first-come, and every row is tested against the exclusions whether or not it matched a material risk.
